why: src/executor.jl:513-518 ("'everything with Φ₀ = 0' is this same gate at index 0, implemented by nothing") and src/model.jl:664-665: boundary zero's updates call the ordinary ticks(0). D-205 widens boundary zero's sweep so every discrete output stage runs (src/executor.jl:524). That widening does not touch the due set, and §6.3 (spec.md:1488-1491) and §14.5 state it.

claim: Staggered stacks never share a boundary, so the worst-case cost of one boundary is a max rather than a sum; a frame's cost is a max too when the stagger is at least a frame
why: src/executor.jl:518 runs a discrete entry only where `(tick - entry.Φ) % entry.D == 0`. Stacks at the same D with distinct Φ never share a tick, so a boundary runs only one stack's entries. | This holds for same-rate stacks, the case §6.3 introduces (spec.md:2138-2141). Stacks at different rates may share a tick: D=2,Φ=0 and D=3,Φ=1 coincide at n=4. 'Stagger at least a frame' must also hold for the cyclic distance D−Φ. With D=10, Φ=8 and a 4-tick frame, the frame (16,20] holds both stacks. Wording could be tightened, but nothing here contradicts the code.
